What this is: a central "shared brain" - our company knowledge (product docs, the company profile, troubleshooting references) hosted once on the proposed server, where every staff AI assistant reads it live. Update a product doc once and every assistant at STA knows it that second. It runs on the server already in this proposal, at no additional monthly cost - the build is my labor, phased over a few weeks of spare cycles.

The problem: every AI assistant we hand out starts going stale on day one

Staff are getting interested in AI assistants, and we can already package one up and hand it over. But each copy carries its own frozen snapshot of company knowledge. When a product doc changes, every copy is wrong until someone re-exports and re-installs it - for every assistant, every time. Five staff assistants means five maintenance chores per update. That treadmill gets worse with every person we onboard, which is exactly backwards.

The fix: knowledge lives in one place; assistants ask it live

What goes central vs. what stays on each person's machine
TierExamplesLives where
Company knowledgeProduct references, troubleshooting guides, Skyward compatibility, research libraryServer (central)
Shared contextCompany profile, team roster, product how-tosServer (central)
System recordsThe catalog of our AI assistants and what each doesServer (central, later phase)
Personal / per-assistantEach assistant's own instructions, each person's preferencesTheir machine (unchanged)

Each staff assistant connects to the server once (a paste-in address plus an access key). From then on, it checks the central library before answering company questions. Nothing to re-download, nothing to re-install, ever.

What STA gets out of it

  • Accuracy: assistants answer from current docs, not last month's copy - fewer confidently wrong answers about our own products.
  • Onboarding speed: a new staff assistant ships with a step-by-step README (download these files, put them here, paste this address) - about 15 minutes, repeatable by anyone, no Adam required.
  • One chore instead of N: knowledge maintenance happens once, centrally, instead of once per person.
  • Control: access is by company-issued key, revocable per person - we always know exactly who can read company knowledge.
  • Compounding value for the server: the same $6-15/mo box now does automation AND knowledge - two returns on one approval.

Assumption stated plainly: staff using AI assistants need their own Claude seats - that is a separate, per-person decision that exists with or without this project. The Shared Brain adds no per-seat software cost.

Rollout - three phases, value at each step

  1. Phase 1 - Build and pilot (first 2-3 weeks): stand up the knowledge service on the server with company knowledge and shared context, read-only, key-protected. Pilot with Adam plus one teammate's assistant.
  2. Phase 2 - Staff rollout: each new staff assistant ships as a package with a plain-English setup README - exact files, exact locations, the connector address, the access key steps. 15 minutes per person, no IT ticket.
  3. Phase 3 - Deepen: add the assistant catalog and shared templates centrally; retire per-copy context files from the export package entirely.

Guardrails

  • Work content only - personal material is excluded by design, with a hard line at the folder level.
  • No customer or student data at launch; anything touching customer data gets a case-by-case review against our CIS Controls work first.
  • Access by named, revocable keys; the access list is reviewed alongside our other security reviews.
How this works under the hood (one paragraph)

The knowledge service is a small MCP server (the open standard Claude uses for connectors) running in Docker on the proposed server, behind HTTPS, exposing search-and-fetch tools over the STA-scope knowledge folders. Staff Coworks add it as a custom connector. Architecture follows the same patterns already researched and documented in our internal knowledge base (MCP server transport, auth, and tool-surface design). Full technical detail will live in the project blueprint once Discovery runs.
